scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

Let me break this down step by step. First, the person is 24, working a minimum wage plus commission job, and doesn't have much savings. Their girlfriend is a student working part-time, barely making ends meet with rent and school fees. They've been dating for three years without major issues except this one. The girlfriend is concerned because the person spends a lot of time and money on their family, which she feels is taking away from building a future together. The person's family is close, and they feel a strong obligation to help them. Their mom recently received a settlement of about $100k, bought a house and a new car, but the person still feels the need to help. The girlfriend doesn't understand why, especially since the family seems financially stable now. She's upset because the person isn't focusing on his own future, like getting a real estate license, which he's been trying to do but can't find the time because of family demands. They had a heated fight where the girlfriend said she feels like the person doesn't care enough about their future together and that she might have to prioritize herself. Now she's talking about saving for her own apartment and car, which makes the person feel like she's wrong for asking him to not help his family. So, is the person being an asshole for putting family first? Let's consider both sides. On one hand, family is important, and it's natural to want to support them. The person feels a strong sense of duty, and their family is close, which adds emotional weight. They're trying to balance this with their relationship, but it's causing tension. On the other hand, the girlfriend is also trying to build a future. She's working hard, managing school and part-time work, and interning. She's not asking him to abandon his family but wants to ensure they have a solid foundation together. The person's focus on family is making her feel neglected and worried about their future. The person mentioned that the family is demanding and gets angry or sad when he's not around. This creates a difficult situation where he feels he can't let them down. However, the girlfriend is feeling like her needs aren't being met, leading her to focus on her own future. I think the issue here is communication and balance. Both partners have valid concerns. The person needs to acknowledge the girlfriend's feelings and work together to find a middle ground. It's not about choosing one over the other but finding a way to support both family and relationship. By telling the girlfriend that family comes first, the person might have made her feel like her needs are secondary, which can be hurtful. It's important to have open conversations about expectations, priorities, and how to support each other without one feeling neglected. So, in this case, the person might be being a bit insensitive by prioritizing family without considering the girlfriend's needs and feelings. It's not necessarily wrong to care for family, but the way it's handled can come across as dismissive of the relationship's future.
